topics.title: Saudi Arabia probes airport defenses
topics.summary: Saudi Arabia opened an investigation into how missiles and drones reached Riyadh's airport, while officials weighed wider regional security concerns after recent Houthi attacks.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a major airport suddenly becomes the center of a security mystery, who wants the technical explanation and who just wants their flight refunded?

topics.title: Nobel laureate backs international courts
topics.summary: Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay urged countries to defend international justice and the broader legal order, saying courts need collective support, not only public praise.
topics.discussionPrompt: When someone says rules only matter if people back them up, who nods like a civics teacher and who asks who enforces the enforcers?

topics.title: Indigenous Peoples Day marked in US
topics.summary: Communities across the United States marked Indigenous Peoples Day with celebrations, protests and calls to rethink how history is taught and remembered.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a holiday asks everyone to look at history from another angle, who gets reflective and who starts planning the community potluck?

topics.title: Ukraine power sites hit again
topics.summary: Ukraine reported Russian attacks on multiple power plants after President Trump claimed an energy ceasefire, while Moscow declined to confirm the reported arrangement.
topics.discussionPrompt: When two sides describe the same supposed deal very differently, who waits for receipts and who starts reading between every line?

topics.title: Indonesia eyes mosque quake alerts
topics.summary: Indonesia is exploring whether mosque loudspeakers could also broadcast earthquake warnings, using familiar community infrastructure to move alerts faster in risky areas.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyday neighborhood speakers could double as emergency tech, who loves the practical shortcut and who worries about false alarms?

topics.title: Pakistan provincial suspension sparks dispute
topics.summary: Imran Khan's party denounced Pakistan's suspension of a provincial government as a coup, adding another flashpoint to the country's already tense political scene.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a political fight turns into an argument over who gets to run the room, who reaches for the constitution and who reaches for tea?

topics.title: EU caps Chinese hybrid imports
topics.summary: The European Union plans to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle imports to 350,000 a year, a move expected to shrink China's market share in Europe.
topics.discussionPrompt: If car rules change the showroom overnight, who talks trade policy and who just asks whether the cup holders are still good?

topics.title: Economists win Nobel for crisis models
topics.summary: American economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford won the Nobel Memorial Prize in economics for work on models used to understand spending, saving and shocks.
topics.discussionPrompt: When economists win for explaining why people spend or save, who says humans are predictable and who points at their own impulse purchases?

topics.title: Markets watch oil and inflation
topics.summary: US stocks hovered near records as oil prices climbed and investors looked ahead to inflation, retail sales and bank earnings reports later this week.
topics.discussionPrompt: When markets look calm but everyone is watching oil prices, who trusts the charts and who starts budgeting for snacks differently?

topics.title: Brewers take NLCS opener
topics.summary: Milwaukee edged Los Angeles 2-1 in the National League Championship Series opener, with Brice Turang homering and the Brewers bullpen protecting the lead.
topics.discussionPrompt: After a tight playoff opener, who becomes instantly superstitious and who insists it is still just one game?
